# AMPL (Amplitude, Inc.) — Technical Analysis Report
**As of 2026-10-13**

## Indicator selection rationale
For a stock in a strong, sustained uptrend like AMPL, I selected complementary indicators across categories: **close_50_sma** and **close_200_sma** (trend confirmation), **rsi** (momentum/overbought), **macd** + **macds** (trend momentum and signal crossovers), **boll_ub** + **boll_lb** (volatility envelope and breakout/overextension zones), and **atr** (volatility for risk sizing). The verified snapshot also provides close_10_ema and macdh, which are incorporated below.

## Trend structure
AMPL has been in a powerful uptrend since the late-July washout. Price bottomed at a closing low of **8.05 on 2026-07-23** after a two-day capitulation (9.59 → 8.74 → 8.05 on heavy volume of 3.9M shares on 07-23), then staged a steady recovery through August and September. The current close of **15.61 on 2026-10-13** represents roughly a 94% gain off that July low — an exceptional run.

The moving-average picture is unambiguously bullish:
- Price (**15.61**) >> 10 EMA (**14.97**) >> 50 SMA (**13.33**) >> 200 SMA (**9.26**)
- All averages are rising; the 50 SMA has climbed from ~11.20 (09-14) to 13.33, and the 200 SMA is trending up from ~8.94 to 9.26 — the long-term trend has fully turned positive.
- The separation between price and the 50 SMA (~17%) is wide, indicating a strong but extended trend.

## Momentum
- **RSI at 70.90** sits just above the classic 70 overbought threshold and has been elevated for five consecutive sessions (70.1, 72.8, 70.3, 70.9 range since 10-06). Notably, price has kept making new highs while RSI peaked at 72.75 on 10-09 and is slightly lower at 70.90 — a mild hint of momentum deceleration, though not a confirmed divergence.
- **MACD (0.71) is above its signal (0.58)** with a positive histogram (0.12). The MACD line has risen every session since late September, confirming trend momentum remains intact. However, the MACD signal line is rising faster in relative terms, narrowing the gap — worth watching for a bearish crossover as an early exit warning.
- **MACD crossed above its signal around 2026-09-30/10-01**, which coincided with the breakout leg from ~13.85 to 15.67 — a fresh buy signal that has so far played out.

## Volatility and bands
- Price (**15.61**) is pressing against the **upper Bollinger Band at 15.93**, with the intraday high of 15.91 touching it on 10-13. The bands are expanding (upper band rising from ~14.19 to 15.93 over the period), which is characteristic of trend acceleration rather than mean reversion — "riding the band" behavior typical of strong trends.
- **ATR at 0.64** (~4.1% of price) has actually *declined* from ~0.69 at end-September even as price rallied — the advance is orderly rather than panic-driven, which is a constructive sign, though it also means ~$0.64 daily swings should be expected for stop placement.
- Volume on the recent leg has been healthy but not climactic (1.7–3.0M on up days vs. 0.9M on 10-13). The light volume on the most recent session is a mild caution — the rally is losing some participation.

## Actionable levels
- **Resistance/overbought zone:** 15.93 (upper Bollinger), then the 16.17 intraday high of 10-12 and psychological 16.00.
- **First support:** 14.97 (10 EMA) — a pullback that holds here is a normal trend continuation pattern.
- **Stronger support:** ~14.20 (Bollinger mid / 20 SMA) and **13.33 (50 SMA)**. A close below the 50 SMA would be the first serious trend warning.
- **Trailing stop guidance:** With ATR ≈ 0.64, a 2×ATR trailing stop (~$1.28 below entry, i.e., ~14.30 from current levels) balances noise vs. protection.

## Risks and caveats
- RSI >70 plus price at the upper band means AMPL is **short-term overbought**; new entries here carry poor risk/reward versus waiting for a pullback toward the 10 EMA or 20 SMA.
- The stock has nearly doubled in under three months — moves of this magnitude frequently see sharp, fast mean-reversion pullbacks (the late-July drop showed it can fall ~15% in two days).
- Declining volume on the latest push and RSI plateauing suggest momentum could be nearing exhaustion in the near term.
- Low-priced stock (~$15) with elevated beta behavior — position sizing should reflect the ~4% daily ATR.

## Summary table

| Aspect | Reading | Signal |
|---|---|---|
| Close (10-13) | $15.61 | — |
| Trend vs MAs | Price > 10EMA > 50SMA > 200SMA, all rising | Strongly bullish |
| RSI | 70.90 | Overbought; watch for divergence |
| MACD / Signal | 0.71 / 0.58, hist +0.12 | Bullish, gap narrowing |
| Bollinger position | At upper band (15.93), bands expanding | Strong trend, extended |
| ATR | 0.64 (~4.1%) | Elevated but declining — orderly rally |
| Support | 14.97 (10EMA), 14.20 (mid-band), 13.33 (50SMA) | Buy zones on pullback |
| Resistance | 15.93 / 16.00–16.17 | Overhead cap zone |
| Volume | 0.9M on 10-13, below recent up-day average | Mild participation caution |
| Overall bias | Bullish trend, tactically overbought | Hold/trim; wait for pullback to add |

# AMPL (Amplitude, Inc.) — Fundamentals Report
**As of 2026-10-13 · SEC EDGAR filings available through this date**

## Company profile
Amplitude, Inc. is a digital analytics software company (product analytics / digital optimization platform). The fundamentals vendor withheld point-in-time profile fields (market cap, multiples, sector) for 2026-10-13 because it only serves present-day values, so valuation data must come from another agent's tools.

## Revenue and growth
Quarterly revenue has grown steadily and is still accelerating in absolute terms:

| Period | Revenue ($M) |
|---|---|
| Q1 2023 | 66 |
| Q3 2024 | 75 |
| Q1 2025 | 83 |
| Q3 2025 | 89 |
| Q4 2025* | 93 |
| Q1 2026 | ~89–93 run-rate; Q2 2026 | 101 |

Latest filed quarter (Q2 2026): **$101M revenue**, up ~26% YoY vs Q2 2025 ($80M). Growth re-accelerated — the 2023–2024 pace was ~8–9% YoY, while 2026 quarters show mid-20s growth. That is the single most important positive signal in the filings.

## Profitability — still loss-making, losses widening again
- Gross margin held around **68–72%** through 2025 but slipped in Q2 2026: gross profit $69M on $101M revenue ≈ **68%**, with cost of revenue jumping to $32M (vs $23–25M in prior quarters) — worth watching; could reflect infrastructure/AI costs or an acquisition mix change.
- Net income: persistently negative. Recent quarters: Q1 2025 −$22M, Q2 2025 −$25M, Q3 2025 −$24M, Q1 2026 −$23M, **Q2 2026 −$35M** — the largest quarterly loss since 2022.
- Diluted EPS: −$0.14 to −$0.19 through 2024–2025, deteriorating to **−$0.27 in Q2 2026**.

## Balance sheet — shrinking cash cushion
- Cash and equivalents peaked at ~$317M (2024-09) and fell to **$74M by Q2 2026** — a steep drawdown.
- Total assets $357M (down from ~$445M in 2024); stockholders' equity dropped to **$136M** from ~$290M a year earlier.
- Liabilities rose to $220M (from ~$175M), mostly current ($210M current liabilities vs $220M current assets — current ratio ≈ 1.05, thin).
- The combination — cash down ~$200M+ in two years, equity halved, liabilities up — suggests either a large buyback/acquisition or sustained burn. The cash flow statement supports the former explanation at least in part.

## Cash flow — operating flow positive on a TTM basis, but big capital returns
- Operating cash flow (cumulative YTD figures): FY2024 ~$15M (9mo), FY2025 $17M (9mo), 2026 YTD: −$12M Q1 then **+$14M by H1** — seasonally Q1-negative, positive thereafter. Capex is minimal (~$1–2M/yr), so OCF ≈ FCF.
- Financing cash flow: −$100M YTD 2026, −$40M FY2025 — heavy share repurchases (or debt repayment) are the main driver of the cash decline, not operating burn.
- Investing cash flow +$79M YTD 2026 — likely liquidation of short-term investments to fund the buybacks.

## Insider transactions
Withheld by the vendor — trades lack filing dates so point-in-time visibility can't be established. No insider signal available.

## Key takeaways for traders
1. **Growth re-acceleration is real**: ~26% YoY revenue growth in 2026 vs high-single-digits in 2024 — a genuine inflection worth a re-rating if sustained.
2. **But losses widened sharply in Q2 2026** (−$35M net, −$0.27 EPS, gross margin compression). If Q3 confirms margin pressure, the growth-is-profitable narrative weakens.
3. **Cash runway is narrowing**: $74M cash, $220M current liabilities, aggressive buybacks (−$100M financing YTD). The company is spending down its balance sheet while unprofitable — a risk if capital markets tighten or growth stalls.
4. **Positive operating cash flow** (~$15–25M/yr) partially offsets the net loss concern — the gap is mostly SBC and non-cash items.
5. Missing data (valuation multiples, insider trades) should be filled by other agents before sizing a position; the fundamental trend is "accelerating growth, deteriorating balance sheet."

bull_history:
Bull Analyst: Let me open this debate with the core fact that reframes everything else: **AMPL's revenue growth has re-accelerated from high-single-digits to ~26% YoY** ($101M in Q2 2026 vs $80M a year ago). For a product-analytics SaaS name, a growth inflection of that magnitude is exactly the kind of event that drives a durable re-rating — and the market is voting with its feet. The stock is up ~94% off the July low, trading at $15.61 with price > 10EMA > 50SMA > 200SMA, all rising. That's not a dead-cat bounce; that's a confirmed trend reversal after a multi-year base.

**Why the growth story has legs:**
- Amplitude sits squarely in the digital-experience/product-analytics stack — the exact category the macro report flags as benefiting from persistent enterprise AI and infrastructure demand narratives. Companies shipping AI features need analytics to measure them; that's a structural tailwind, not a fad.
- The acceleration is sequential and absolute — $75M (Q3'24) → $89M (Q3'25) → $101M (Q2'26). This isn't one good quarter; it's an upward staircase.
- Operating cash flow is **positive** (~$14M H1 2026, $15–25M/yr pace). The GAAP net loss is largely SBC and non-cash noise — the core business actually generates cash, which is precisely the quality screen the market is rewarding right now (see Accenture, IBM getting bid up on FCF).

**Now let me preempt the bear case, because I know what's coming:**

*"The net loss widened to −$35M in Q2."* True — but OCF stayed positive, meaning the gap is non-cash. And management spending into a growth inflection while staying OCF-positive is aggressive but defensible. If Q3 shows the loss narrowing on continued 20%+ growth, this concern evaporates.

*"Cash fell from $317M to $74M."* Look at the cash flow statement: financing outflows were −$100M YTD 2026 while investing inflows were +$79M — the drawdown is **share repurchases**, not operating burn. A management team buying back stock while growth accelerates is signaling confidence, not distress. You can debate the capital allocation, but this isn't a company bleeding out; it's a company choosing to return capital while the engine improves.

*"Technicals show overbought."* RSI at 70.9 with price riding an expanding upper Bollinger Band describes a strong trend, not a broken one — ATR actually *declined* during the rally, meaning the advance is orderly. And here's the part bears ignore: you don't need to buy at $15.61. The report itself maps clean accumulation zones at $14.97 (10EMA) and $14.20 (mid-band). Overbought is a timing note, not a thesis killer.

*"The tape is late-cycle; BlackRock is cautious."* Fair — and that's why AMPL's own fundamentals matter more, not less. In a market rotating toward FCF-positive, genuinely-growing software, AMPL screens *better* than the unprofitable-duration names getting sold. The ~5.9% yield tripwire is a real macro risk for ALL equities; it's not an AMPL-specific argument.

**The sentiment kicker:** retail chatter frames AMPL as an "undiscovered multi-year breakout" with only ~1,745 StockTwits watchers. Zero bearish posts, constructive-not-euphoric tone. That means the crowd hasn't piled in yet — there's still discovery left in this move.

**Bottom line:** accelerating growth (+26% YoY), positive operating cash flow, a confirmed technical reversal off a multi-year base, an AI-analytics tailwind, and a still-underfollowed stock. The bear can point at GAAP losses and a thinner cash cushion, but those are symptoms of buybacks and SBC, not a deteriorating business. Pullbacks toward $14–15 are opportunities, not warnings. The bull case isn't that AMPL is perfect — it's that the market is only beginning to price a real growth inflection. Bring on the rebuttal.
bear_history:
Bear Analyst: Bear Analyst: Let's start where the bull wants to end — with that 26% growth number, because it's the only real card in the deck, and it's being played far too confidently.

**The growth re-acceleration is being funded, not earned.** Revenue jumped to $101M while the net loss *widened* to −$35M — the worst quarterly loss since 2022 — and gross margin *fell* from ~72% to ~68% as cost of revenue spiked from ~$24M to $32M. The bull frames this as "spending into an inflection." Read it the other way: the incremental revenue is coming at deteriorating unit economics. If growth requires margin compression, the "re-rating" story is backwards — that's what growth *deceleration* looks like when the spend gets pulled. And "if Q3 shows losses narrowing" is doing a lot of work in the bull thesis. If, if, if. The actual evidence in hand is a widening loss, not a narrowing one.

**The buyback defense is the weakest part of the bull case.** Yes, the cash decline is partly repurchases — that's not exoneration, that's an indictment. Management burned ~$200M of the balance sheet, dropped equity from ~$290M to $136M, and now sits on $74M cash against $220M in current liabilities — a current ratio of ~1.05. They bought back stock while unprofitable, while margins were compressing, and at prices that, before July, were collapsing toward $8. That's not "signaling confidence"; that's capital allocation malpractice that has left the company one bad quarter away from a liquidity problem. A company with 1.05x current assets coverage does not have room for error — and there's no insider-transaction data available to confirm management is even holding, let alone buying personally.

**On "OCF is positive so losses are just SBC":** +$14M in H1 on $190M of H1 revenue is a ~7% FCF margin at best — thin, seasonal (Q1 was −$12M), and insufficient to fund the buyback pace or cover GAAP losses. And SBC is not "noise" — it's real dilution being paid to employees, which is part of why the share count math and equity figures keep deteriorating. Calling a $35M quarterly net loss "non-cash noise" is exactly the framing that gets investors hurt in SaaS names.

**The technicals argue for a pullback, not a position.** The bull's own report concedes: RSI >70 for five straight sessions *with RSI making a lower high while price made a higher high* — that's textbook momentum divergence forming, not a quibble. MACD signal converging, volume on the latest push at 0.9M versus 1.7–3.0M on prior up days — participation is drying up at the highs. Price is pinned to the upper Bollinger with 17% separation from the 50 SMA. The bull says "buy at $14.97 or $14.20" — fine, but that concedes ~$1.40 of downside to fair entry, i.e., the tape itself says current holders are buying exhaustion. And remember: this stock dropped 15% in two days in July. A 94% run in under three months on a low-priced, high-beta name is precisely the setup for a violent mean reversion, not a "durable re-rating."

**The macro math the bull waved away is the sharpest knife.** This is a tape where BlackRock is turning cautious, fund managers have a defined ~5.9% yield tripwire, and money is rotating *toward profitable FCF generators* (IBM, Accenture) and *away* from duration-heavy story stocks. AMPL is unprofitable on a GAAP basis, margin-compressing, and balance-sheet-depleted — it screens into the bucket being sold, not bought. "Macro risk affects everyone" is true and irrelevant: high-multiple, low-liquidity names fall fastest when multiples compress. There is also zero confirmed AMPL-specific news this week — the rally is technically driven with no identifiable catalyst, which means there's no fundamental floor underneath it.

**The sentiment point actually cuts against the bull.** Seven StockTwits messages, two sources entirely unavailable, and the "undiscovered breakout" narrative is classic momentum-chaser framing — the posts are literally congratulating holders, which means the easy money was already made by whoever owned at $9–11. Thin chatter plus a vertical chart is not discovery; it's the echo of a move that's already happened.

**Bottom line:** The bull is asking you to pay $15.61 — 94% off the low, RSI extended, volume fading, RSI diverging — for a company with a worsening GAAP loss, compressing gross margin, a current ratio of ~1.05, and $74M of cash against an aggressive buyback habit, in a macro regime actively punishing exactly this profile. Even if the growth is real, the correct action in the data is the technical report's own conclusion: this is a hold/trim, not a buy. The downside map is concrete ($14.97 → $14.20 → $13.33, with July showing −15% in two days); the upside requires Q3 to deliver a margin recovery there's currently no evidence for. Risk/reward at current levels belongs to the bears.
investment_plan:
**Recommendation**: Underweight

**Rationale**: The bear side carried this round, not because the bull's growth story is fake but because it was won on price, timing, and balance sheet rather than on direction. The bull's strongest card — a genuine re-acceleration to ~26% YoY revenue with positive operating cash flow — is real, and it's why this isn't a Sell. But the bear dismantled the supporting pillars: the cash decline wasn't benign capital return so much as ~$200M of buybacks executed while unprofitable and margin-compressing, leaving $74M cash against $220M current liabilities (~1.05x coverage) — no margin for error. Gross margin fell from ~72% to ~68% even as revenue grew, meaning the incremental growth is arriving at worse unit economics, and the bull's counter ('Q3 will show losses narrowing') is an unverified hope, not evidence. On the tape, the bull effectively conceded the bear's point by mapping fair entries at $14.97 and $14.20 — below the $15.61 price — while RSI divergence, fading volume, and a 94% run in under three months argue the current print is exhaustion, not entry. In a macro regime rotating toward profitable FCF names and away from unprofitable duration stories, AMPL screens into the wrong bucket at the wrong price. Net: the business inflection is credible, but the risk/reward at $15.61 belongs to the bears — trim, don't chase, and let Q3 prove the margin story before re-adding.

**Strategic Actions**: 1) Trim AMPL to roughly half of a standard allocation at current levels (~$15.61); do not add here. The residual position keeps exposure to the genuine growth inflection in case Q3 confirms margin recovery. 2) Set limit re-entry zones at $14.97 (10EMA) and more aggressively at $14.20 (mid-band) — only restore toward full size if price pulls back into those zones and holds, rather than chasing strength. 3) Implement a hard stop near $13.33 (next mapped support); this name dropped 15% in two days in July and a 1.05 current ratio means a bad quarter can gap hard. 4) Make the Q3 earnings print the decision gate: re-upgrade only if revenue growth holds >20% AND net loss narrows AND gross margin stabilizes/recovers toward ~70%; if loss widens again or margin compresses further, exit the remainder. 5) Watch the macro tripwire: if the 10Y yield approaches ~5.9%, cut exposure faster — unprofitable, low-liquidity SaaS gets sold first in multiple compression. 6) Note the evidence gap: no insider-transaction data was available; if insider selling surfaces alongside the buyback-funded narrative, that further supports the trim.
